restoration_note: The teaching enumerates four works accomplished when the Third Ambassador (the Lord's call) manifests his image to the rational: (1) image shown forth in glory; (2) all gates of the firmaments opened then shut again; (3) light and discriminating sight chosen out, exceeding ordinary light; (4) manifestation in the perfection of the men of Christ — light prepared for the living soul, with a hidden chamber set within the worlds of enmity. The fills are tightly constrained by the formulaic ordinal pattern (ⲧⲧϣⲁⲣⲡ, ⲧⲧⲙⲁⲍⲥⲛⲉⲩ, ⲧⲧⲙⲁⲍϣⲁⲙⲧ, ⲧⲧⲙⲁⲍⲭⲧⲁⲩ), the repeating ⲟⲩⲁⲛⲍ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ formula, and the cosmological vocabulary ⲥⲧⲉⲣⲉⲱⲙⲁ / ⲣⲱⲩⲉ. Gap {15} (8-char lacuna with only trailing ⲉ) and the small gap {8} (an unconstrained slot inside ⲍⲙ ⲡⲥⲏⲩ) are too weakly anchored to fill responsibly.

coptic_restorations.basis: Completes ⲟⲩⲱⲛⲍ / ⲟⲩⲁⲛⲍ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'manifest forth'; standard Lycopolitan formula for the Ambassador's revelation.
Completes ⲍⲱⲃ 'work, deed' — the four great works (ⲭⲧⲁⲩ ⲛ̄ⲛⲁⲃ ⲛ̄ⲍⲱⲃ).
Completes the verb begun on the previous line: ⲟⲩ-/ⲁⲛⲍ → ⲟⲩⲁⲛⲍ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'manifest forth' (Lycopolitan vowel ⲁ for Sahidic ⲱ).
Ordinal 'first' for feminine ⲧⲉⲭⲍⲓⲕⲱⲛ — ⲧⲧϣⲁⲣⲡ ⲡⲉ matching the parallel ⲧⲧⲙⲁⲍⲥⲛⲉⲩ ⲡⲉ in 1945.
ⲍⲛ ⲟⲩⲍⲓⲕⲱⲛ ⲛ̄ⲉⲁⲩ 'in an image of glory' — phrase carries into next segment where ⲉⲁⲩ is preserved.
Genitive linker for ⲟⲩⲍⲓⲕⲱⲛ ⲛ̄ⲉⲁⲩ 'image of glory'.
Completes ⲥⲧⲉⲣⲉⲱⲙⲁ 'firmament' (lexicon: structural_term, established) — boundary between discrete degrees, opened during the Ambassador's work.
Completes ⲥⲧⲉⲣⲉⲱⲙⲁ — final syllable carrying onto this line.
Marker placed inside the standard temporal phrase ⲍⲙ ⲡⲥⲏⲩ ⲉⲧⲙⲙⲉⲩ 'at that time'; nothing additional is grammatically required between ⲡ and ⲥⲏⲩ. Likely empty/scribal.
Completes ⲥⲉⲟⲩⲉⲛ 'they are opened', parallel to ⲉⲧⲁⲩⲟⲩⲉⲛ above.
With preserved ⲩⲉ → ⲛⲣⲱⲩⲉ 'the doors/gates' (plural of ⲣⲟ; lexicon: structural_term gate). Restores subject of ⲥⲉϣⲧⲉⲙ 'they are shut': 'the doors again are shut'.
Ordinal 'third' — ⲧⲧⲙⲁⲍϣⲁⲙⲧ ⲡⲉ, parallel to ⲧⲧⲙⲁⲍⲥⲛⲉⲩ ⲡⲉ above; ⲍϣⲁⲙⲧ preserved.
Completes ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲛⲉ 'the light' (Lycopolitan for ⲡⲟⲩⲟⲉⲓⲛ); coordinated with ⲧⲃⲓⲛⲣ̄ⲃⲁⲗ 'looking-out' (discrimination).
'chosen-out of the image' — the discriminating sight is drawn from the manifested image; carries forward the ⲍⲓⲕⲱⲛ thread from the first work and sets up the comparison 'that light exceeds...'.
Comparative phrase ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ ⲉⲧⲙⲙⲉⲩ ⲣⲍⲟⲩⲟ ⲡⲁⲣⲁ ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ 'that light exceeds the [ordinary] light'; preserved ⲡ confirms article and following ⲡⲁⲣⲁ ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ confirms the lexeme.
8-char lacuna with only a final ⲉ visible amid scattered traces; comparative clause about the ordinary light is too unconstrained to restore responsibly.
Ordinal 'fourth' — ⲧⲧⲙⲁⲍⲭⲧⲁⲩ ⲡⲉ, completing the four-step pattern; ⲍⲭⲧⲁⲩ preserved.
ⲁⲭⲟⲩⲁⲛⲍ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'he manifested forth' (Lycopolitan ⲟⲩⲁⲛⲍ); ⲁⲭ and ⲛⲍ preserved bracket the missing ⲟⲩⲁ.
With preserved ⲁⲓ̈ → ⲡⲁⲓ̈ 'this' — demonstrative subject: ⲡⲁⲓ̈ ⲛⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ 'this is a light'.
Partial trace ⲩⲃⲧⲏ within a 5-char gap suggests ⲥⲟⲩⲃⲧⲏ / ⲥⲃⲧⲱⲧ 'prepared'; verb takes dative ⲛ̄ⲧⲯⲩⲭⲏ 'for the soul'. Reading: ⲁⲭⲥⲟⲩⲃⲧⲏ ⲛ̄ⲧⲯⲩⲭⲏ 'he prepared for the soul'.
Completes ⲡⲣⲓⲉ 'shine' from preceding ⲧⲉⲧⲁⲥⲧⲣ̄ⲡ-, then preposition ⲍⲛ̄ governing ⲟⲩⲭⲱⲕ: 'who shone-forth in a perfection'.
Indefinite article: ⲟⲩⲙⲁ ⲛ̄ⲍⲏⲡ → ⲟⲩⲙⲁⲍⲁⲓⲡⲉ 'a hidden place/chamber'; ⲩⲙⲁⲍⲁⲓⲡⲉ preserved.

english_restorations.basis: Restored Coptic ⲛⲣⲱⲩⲉ 'the doors/gates' supplies the explicit subject of ⲥⲉϣⲧⲉⲙ 'they are shut'; lexicon ⲣⲟ = gate.
Restored ⲛ̄ⲧⲉⲭⲍⲓⲕⲱⲛ links the chosen-out light/sight back to the image manifested in the first work; renders the source from which discrimination is drawn.
The 8-char lacuna following ⲉⲧⲉϣⲁϥ- (relative habitual) is too weakly constrained — only a final ⲉ trace — to assign an English equivalent.
Restored ⲁⲭⲥⲟⲩⲃⲧⲏ from partial trace ⲩⲃⲧⲏ — verb ⲥⲃⲧⲱⲧ 'prepare', taking dative ⲛ̄ⲧⲯⲩⲭⲏ 'for the soul'; consonant with the fourth work's laying-down of a chamber for the living soul.
